title: Red Sox first baseman Triston Casas undergoes left wrist surgery in latest setback
content:
Boston Red Sox first baseman Triston Casas underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left wrist Thursday, the latest setback in his attempt to return from a knee procedure last year.

Casas, a first-round pick of the Red Sox in 2018, has not played since rupturing his left patellar tendon while trying to beat out a single on May 2, 2025. He had surgery to repair his knee and missed the remainder of the season, focusing on returning this spring. However, when he began to swing a bat in spring training, he developed an abdominal strain and was shut down. After a slow ramp-up from that injury, he developed wrist inflammation that has lingered into the summer.

The team, which announced his surgery Thursday, did not provide a timeline for his return.

Casas has sustained several injuries since finishing third in American League Rookie of the Year voting in 2023, when he hit .263 with an .856 OPS and 24 homers in 132 games. The following season, he spent 99 games on the injured list after tearing a rib cartilage on a swing, and played in just 29 games in 2025.
